deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivation and no numbers apart from the folio number 209. It continues the scheme begun on fol. 208, headed 'Fortsetzung der Epaillyschen Dreiecke, von der Seite Bentheim–Kirchhesepe bis Ostfriesland'. That heading means the continuation of the triangles of the French engineer-geographer Epailly, running from the side Bentheim–Kirchhesepe to East Frisia.

On fol. 208 the first stations (Bentheim, Kirchhesepe, Ulsen, Coeverden) carry tabulated data:
- the observed direction;
- a correction in seconds;
- the corrected direction;
- the log of the side length.

The later stations there, and all stations on this page, are only skeleton entries. Gauss writes each station name, underlined, and below it the stations sighted from it. The data columns were presumably meant to be filled in later; that is my inference.

The network recorded here, as station: target stations:
- Rolde: Beilen, Gröningen [Groningen], Onstwedde, Sleen.
- Onstwedde: Sleen, Rolde, Gröningen, Midwolde, Leer.
- Gröningen: Midwolde, Onstwedde, Rolde.
- Midwolde: Gröningen, Emden, Leer, Onstwedde.
- Leer: Onstwedde, Midwolde, Emden, Aurich, Strackhold, Westerstede.
- Emden: Midwolde, Aurich, Leer.
- Aurich: Leer, Emden, Strackhold.

In graph terms this is an adjacency list. Vertices are trigonometric stations; edges are observed lines of sight.

The triangles it implies include:
- Rolde–Onstwedde–Gröningen
- Rolde–Onstwedde–Sleen
- Onstwedde–Gröningen–Midwolde
- Onstwedde–Midwolde–Leer
- Midwolde–Leer–Emden
- Leer–Emden–Aurich
- Leer–Aurich–Strackhold
- Leer–Strackhold–Westerstede, completed on fol. 210

The chain thus carries the French (Epailly / Krayenhoff-related) triangulation from Drenthe and Groningen across the Ems to Leer, Emden and Aurich. From there it continues on fol. 210 toward Jever, Varel, Oldenburg and Bremen. That is the link Gauss needed to tie the Dutch and French triangulation into his Hanoverian degree measurement.

What is computed: nothing on this page. It is an organisational scaffold (a station and direction index) for a later station adjustment.
errors: No computational errors are possible, since the page has no computation.

Consistency check: every line of sight is listed reciprocally (A under B whenever B under A) across fols. 208–210, e.g. Rolde–Sleen, Onstwedde–Leer, Midwolde–Emden, Leer–Westerstede, Aurich–Strackhold. No inconsistency was found.

results.what: Station-by-station list of observed directions (network skeleton) for the Epailly triangle chain from Drenthe/Groningen to East Frisia (Leer, Emden, Aurich).
results.modern_name: Triangulation network adjacency list / station index for direction adjustment
results.usually_credited_to: Standard geodetic bookkeeping; the underlying observations are due to Epailly (French survey of NW Germany, Napoleonic era)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bare list of triangulation station names. It is well known that Gauss used Epailly's and Krayenhoff's triangles to connect his Hanoverian survey to the Dutch net. Nothing mathematical is present.

transcription_corrections: The transcription is accurate. Station headers (underlined) are Rolde, Onstwedde, Gröningen, Midwolde, Leer, Emden and Aurich; the other names are targets sighted from them.
'Gröningen' is written with an umlaut in the manuscript (i.e. Groningen); 'Strackhold' is the station near Strackholt in East Frisia.
The folio number '209' is at the top right.
